test_scenarios.name: Connection Singleton Guard - Concurrent Connect Calls
test_scenarios.description: Verify that multiple concurrent calls to BridgeSocketManager.connect() from different entry points (chrome.storage.onChanged, chrome.alarms.onAlarm, manual trigger) result in only ONE WebSocket connection being created, not multiple competing connections.

setup.environment: Unit test with mocked Chrome APIs

steps: Create a BridgeSocketManager instance with mocked WebSocket that counts constructor calls
Call connect() from 3 concurrent 'threads' (using Promise.resolve().then() chains)
Verify WebSocket constructor was called exactly ONCE
Verify all 3 callers received the same connection success event
After connection, call connect() again - verify it's a no-op (no new WebSocket)
Simulate connection drop, then call connect() from 2 entry points simultaneously - verify only one reconnect attempt
expected_results: WebSocket constructor call count: 1 (not 3)
All concurrent callers resolve with same connected state
Second connect() call during CONNECTED state is immediate no-op
Reconnect after disconnect spawns exactly one new WebSocket

test_scenarios.name: Connection Singleton Guard - SW Restart State Recovery
test_scenarios.description: Verify that after a Chrome MV3 Service Worker restart, the connection state is properly recovered from chrome.storage.session and only one reconnect is attempted, not a storm of concurrent connects.

setup.environment: Unit test with mocked Chrome APIs simulating SW restart

steps: Establish a connection (WebSocket open, state = CONNECTED)
Simulate SW restart: clear all JS state (this.socket = null, this.state = DISCONNECTED)
Simulate chrome.storage.session containing saved instanceId
Fire chrome.alarms.onAlarm (keepalive) AND chrome.storage.onChanged simultaneously
Verify only ONE connect() is in-flight at a time
Verify connection is re-established successfully
Verify instanceId is preserved across restart
expected_results: No 'Cannot construct WebSocket' errors from multiple concurrent attempts
Single WebSocket connection re-established
instanceId from chrome.storage.session is used (not regenerated)
Connection state machine transitions: DISCONNECTED -> CONNECTING -> CONNECTED

test_scenarios.name: TTL Cleanup - Server-Side Idle Connection Auto-Close
test_scenarios.description: Verify that the server-side Durable Object closes a WebSocket connection that has been idle (no PING/PONG/any message) for more than 45 seconds, and clears the activeConnection state.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker OR isolated DO test harness
setup.timing: 45s idle threshold + 15s keepalive interval = ~60s total test time

steps: Connect a WebSocket to /bridge with valid token
Send SESSION_READY to establish session
Do NOT send any messages for 46+ seconds (no PING responses either)
Verify server closes the connection (onclose fires with code 1000, reason 'Stale connection')
Verify activeConnection is null after close
Verify a new connection from same instanceId is accepted (not 409)
expected_results: After 46s idle: WebSocket onclose fires with close code 1000
Server log shows: '[Bridge DO] Socket idle >45s, closing as stale'
activeConnection === null after cleanup
New connection from same instanceId: accepted (reconnect)
test_scenarios.note: Can be accelerated in test by temporarily setting idle threshold to 5s

test_scenarios.name: TTL Cleanup - Client-Side Stale Socket Detection
test_scenarios.description: Verify that the client-side BridgeSocketManager detects a stale connection (open WebSocket but no messages for 60s) and initiates a reconnect.

setup.environment: Unit test with mocked WebSocket and timers

steps: Create BridgeSocketManager, connect() succeeds
Mock WebSocket to be 'open' but never deliver messages
Advance timer past 60s idle threshold
Verify manager transitions to RECONNECTING state
Verify reconnect attempt is made
After successful reconnect, verify state returns to CONNECTED
expected_results: After 60s idle: state changes from CONNECTED to RECONNECTING
Reconnect attempt scheduled
On successful reconnect: state returns to CONNECTED
reconnectAttempts counter incremented appropriately

test_scenarios.name: Instance ID Tracking - Same Instance Reconnect
test_scenarios.description: Verify that when the same extension instance (same instanceId) reconnects after a disconnect, the server accepts the connection and properly replaces the old socket.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker
setup.identity: Single instanceId used for both connections

steps: Connect WebSocket with instanceId=A, token=valid
Send SESSION_READY to establish session state
Close the WebSocket (normal close, code 1000)
Immediately connect a new WebSocket with same instanceId=A
Verify connection is ACCEPTED (not 409)
Verify old socket was closed by server (if still open)
Verify new connection receives session state or requests sync
expected_results: First connection: 101 Switching Protocols (accepted)
Second connection with same instanceId: 101 (accepted, reconnect)
Server log shows: 'Same device reconnecting - closing old connection'
No 409 Conflict returned for same-instance reconnect

test_scenarios.name: Instance ID Tracking - Different Instance, Stale Old Connection
test_scenarios.description: Verify that when a DIFFERENT instanceId connects and the old connection is stale (idle >45s), the server treats the old connection as stale, closes it, and accepts the new connection.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker
setup.identity: instanceId=A for first connection, instanceId=B for second

steps: Connect WebSocket with instanceId=A
Leave connection idle for 46+ seconds (no messages)
Verify server closes connection A as stale (on server side)
Connect new WebSocket with instanceId=B (different instance, same token)
Verify connection B is ACCEPTED (not 409)
Verify server log shows stale detection and replacement
expected_results: Connection A closed by server after 45s idle (stale cleanup)
Connection B from different instanceId: accepted (old was stale)
NOT a 409 - server recognized old connection was dead

test_scenarios.name: Instance ID Tracking - Different Instance, Healthy Old Connection (Genuine 409)
test_scenarios.description: Verify that when a DIFFERENT instanceId tries to connect while the old connection is still HEALTHY (recent activity), the server correctly rejects with 409 Conflict.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker
setup.identity: instanceId=A for first connection, instanceId=B for second

steps: Connect WebSocket with instanceId=A
Send PONG responses to keep connection healthy (within 45s window)
Attempt to connect new WebSocket with instanceId=B (same token)
Verify server returns 409 Conflict
Verify server log shows: 'Rejected connection from secondary device'
Verify original connection A remains healthy and active
expected_results: Connection B: HTTP 409 Conflict returned
Connection A: remains open and healthy
Server correctly distinguishes 'reconnect' from 'new device'
This is the GENUINE 409 case that should still be rejected
test_scenarios.verification_goal: Confirm 409 still correctly rejected for genuine conflicts

test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Multiple Requests on Same Connection
test_scenarios.description: Verify that multiple concurrent requests (EXECUTE_REQUEST, PREPARE_MODEL, PREPARE_SCOPE) can be multiplexed over a single WebSocket connection without requiring reconnection.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker OR unit test with mocked DO

steps: Connect WebSocket, send SESSION_READY with tokens
Send PREPARE_MODEL for model X, wait for MODEL_READY
While model is preparing, send a second PREPARE_MODEL for model Y
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST for conversation 1
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST for conversation 2 (different requestId)
Send PREPARE_SCOPE for notebook scope
Verify all requests are handled concurrently without connection drops
Verify response streams are correctly routed to waiting handlers
expected_results: All requests use the same WebSocket connection (no reconnect triggered)
Each requestId gets its own response handler
No 409 errors from concurrent request handling
STREAM_CHUNK, STREAM_DONE, STREAM_ERROR correctly delivered to respective handlers

test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Scope Switch Without Reconnect
test_scenarios.description: Verify that switching scope (app -> notebook, or app -> app:conversationId) happens over the existing WebSocket connection without requiring a reconnect.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker with mock tab coordinator

steps: Connect WebSocket, establish SESSION_READY with scope='app'
Send PREPARE_SCOPE with target='notebook:abc123'
Verify SCOPE_READY response received on SAME WebSocket
Verify no WebSocket close/reconnect occurred
Verify currentScope on server is updated to 'notebook:abc123'
Send another PREPARE_SCOPE to 'app:conv456'
Verify second scope switch also completes without reconnect
expected_results: Scope switch completes over existing connection
No onclose/onopen cycle during scope switch
Server currentScope updated correctly
PREPARE_SCOPE -> SCOPE_READY round-trip succeeds

test_scenarios.name: Edge Case - Service Worker Restart and Re-establish
test_scenarios.description: End-to-end simulation of a Chrome MV3 Service Worker restart: connection drops without close frame, SW restarts, reads state from chrome.storage.session, and re-establishes connection with same instanceId.

setup.environment: Full integration test with Chrome extension loaded in test browser OR simulated environment

steps: Load extension, establish WebSocket connection to staging worker
Send SESSION_READY, verify session established
Simulate SW restart: all JS state lost (socket=null, state=disconnected)
Simulate SW startup: reads instanceId from chrome.storage.session
SW automatically calls connect() (from startup code or alarm)
New WebSocket connects with SAME instanceId
Server sees same instanceId, accepts reconnect
Extension sends SESSION_READY to re-establish session state
Verify full functionality restored (can send EXECUTE_REQUEST successfully)
expected_results: SW restart does NOT cause 409 (same instanceId reconnects)
Connection re-established within 5 seconds of restart
Session state re-synchronized (protocol version, model catalog)
No user-visible error; extension continues working
test_scenarios.note: Requires Chrome extension test environment or manual verification with browser devtools

test_scenarios.name: Edge Case - Network Blip (Transient Connection Loss)
test_scenarios.description: Simulate a brief network interruption (TCP connection drop) and verify the client detects the disconnect, waits for the network to recover, and reconnects successfully without triggering a 409.

setup.environment: Integration test with network simulation OR manual test with browser devtools throttling

steps: Establish stable WebSocket connection to staging worker
Send periodic PONG responses to keep connection healthy
Simulate network drop: block WebSocket traffic for 5 seconds
Client onclose fires (connection lost)
Client transitions to RECONNECTING, schedules reconnect with backoff
Restore network (unblock WebSocket traffic)
Client reconnect attempt succeeds
Server accepts reconnect (same instanceId, old connection was dropped)
Verify session recovery: protocol version synced, can send requests
expected_results: Network blip detected: onclose fires with appropriate code
Client reconnect triggered after backoff (not immediate storm)
Server accepts reconnect (old socket was dead, same instanceId)
No 409 for network blip reconnect
Session recovers automatically
test_scenarios.note: Can be tested with Chrome devtools Network throttling or tc/netem in staging

test_scenarios.name: Edge Case - 409 Handling Improvement Verification
test_scenarios.description: Comprehensive verification that 409 Conflict is STILL correctly returned for genuine conflicts (different device, different token, or different instance with healthy existing connection), while NOT being returned incorrectly for legitimate reconnects.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker with multiple WebSocket clients

steps: For each row in the matrix above:
1. Set up the 'old connection' state as specified
2. Attempt a new WebSocket connection with the specified parameters
3. Record the HTTP status code returned
4. Verify against expected result
Verify server logs correctly identify the reason for each decision
Verify instanceId is logged on every connection accept/reject event
expected_results: Matrix row 1 (same_id, stale): ACCEPT - reconnect after stale cleanup
Matrix row 2 (same_id, healthy): ACCEPT - reconnect replaces old
Matrix row 3 (diff_id, stale): ACCEPT - stale connection replaced
Matrix row 4 (diff_id, healthy): 409 - GENUINE conflict, correctly rejected
Matrix row 5 (diff_token): 401 - authentication failure
All decisions logged with instanceId for audit trail
test_scenarios.verification_goal: Verify 409 still correctly rejected for genuine conflicts

test_scenarios.name: Edge Case - Extension Reinstall (New Instance ID)
test_scenarios.description: Verify that when the extension is reinstalled (new instanceId generated, chrome.storage.session cleared), the server accepts the new connection because the old instance is no longer active (browser restart clears old socket).

setup.environment: Manual test or simulated environment

steps: Install extension, establish connection with instanceId=A
Close browser completely (clears chrome.storage.session, closes sockets)
Reinstall extension (or clear extension data and reload)
New instanceId=B is generated
Connect with instanceId=B
Server has no active connection for instanceId=A (browser was closed)
Verify connection accepted (not 409)
Verify server treats this as a fresh connection
expected_results: New instanceId accepted (no existing healthy connection to conflict with)
Not a 409 - this is a legitimate new installation
Server starts fresh with new instance
test_scenarios.note: Requires manual browser testing or simulated extension environment

test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Single WS Carries 3 Scopes Simultaneously
test_scenarios.description: Verify that a single WebSocket connection can carry message traffic for 3 different scopes (app, app:conv-X, notebook:Y) concurrently without scope collision or cross-contamination. Each scope maintains its own session state, streaming handlers, and model preparation state.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker with mocked extension that simulates 3 scope sessions

steps: Connect WebSocket with instanceId=A, send SESSION_READY with scope='app'
Send PREPARE_SCOPE for 'app:conv-a1b2c3' - verify SCOPE_READY received, currentScope updated
Send PREPARE_SCOPE for 'notebook:ntb-456def' - verify SCOPE_READY received
Verify server tracks all 3 scopes as active session contexts (not just currentScope)
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST with scope='app' - verify routed to app handler
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST with scope='app:conv-a1b2c3' - verify routed to conversation handler, NOT app handler
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST with scope='notebook:ntb-456def' - verify routed to notebook handler
Verify each requestId's response is delivered to the correct scope's waiting handler
Verify no scope cross-contamination: app:conv response does not leak to app handler
Verify server log shows 3 active scope sessions for this instanceId
expected_results: Single WebSocket connection carries all 3 scopes (no reconnect triggered)
Each scope has independent session state (conversationId, responseId, choiceId per scope)
EXECUTE_REQUEST for app:conv-a1b2c3 does NOT route to app handler
EXECUTE_REQUEST for notebook:ntb-456def does NOT route to app handler
STREAM_CHUNK for notebook scope is not delivered to app:conv handler
Server maintains scopeSessions Map with 3 entries for this instanceId
currentScope reflects the MOST RECENT scope switch, but other scopes remain active
test_scenarios.note: Requires server-side scopeSessions Map (multi-scope session state). Currently only currentScope is tracked - this test validates the multi-scope enhancement.

test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Scope Subscribe/Unsubscribe Mid-Session
test_scenarios.description: Verify that scopes can be dynamically subscribed (PREPARE_SCOPE) and unsubscribed (SCOPE_UNSUBSCRIBE or scope cleanup on navigation away) during an active session, without disrupting other active scopes or the WebSocket connection.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker

steps: Connect WebSocket, establish SESSION_READY with scope='app'
Subscribe to scope 'app:conv-a1b2c3' via PREPARE_SCOPE - verify SCOPE_READY
Subscribe to scope 'notebook:ntb-456def' via PREPARE_SCOPE - verify SCOPE_READY
Verify both scopes are in the active scopeSessions map
Simulate user navigating away from notebook tab (extension sends SCOPE_UNSUBSCRIBE or navigates to different scope)
Verify notebook:ntb-456def is removed from active scopeSessions
Verify app and app:conv-a1b2c3 scopes remain active and functional
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to app:conv-a1b2c3 - verify it still works after notebook unsubscribe
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to app - verify it still works
Subscribe to a NEW scope 'app:conv-new789' - verify it works without affecting existing scopes
Unsubscribe from app:conv-a1b2c3 - verify it's removed, other scopes unaffected
Verify WebSocket remains open throughout all subscribe/unsubscribe operations
expected_results: Scope subscribe (PREPARE_SCOPE -> SCOPE_READY) adds scope to active sessions
Scope unsubscribe removes scope from active sessions without disrupting others
WebSocket connection remains stable throughout (no onclose events)
Active scope count decreases correctly after unsubscribe
Remaining scopes continue to receive messages correctly
No STREAM_ERROR for remaining scopes after another scope unsubscribes
Server log shows scope added/removed events with scope ID
test_scenarios.note: Requires server-side scope unsubscribe handling. Extension sends SCOPE_UNSUBSCRIBE or navigates away; server cleans up scope session.

test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Reconnect Preserves All Scope Sessions
test_scenarios.description: Verify that after a WebSocket reconnect (SW restart, network blip, or deliberate disconnect), all previously active scope sessions are preserved and re-established, not lost. The extension retransmits scope state for each active scope.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker with mocked extension

steps: Connect WebSocket, establish SESSION_READY with scope='app'
Subscribe to app:conv-a1b2c3 and notebook:ntb-456def (3 scopes active)
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to each scope - verify all 3 work
Simulate disconnect: close WebSocket (normal close, code 1000)
Simulate SW restart: extension reinitializes, retrieves instanceId from chrome.storage.session
Extension reconnects with SAME instanceId
Extension sends SESSION_READY with full scope list: ['app', 'app:conv-a1b2c3', 'notebook:ntb-456def']
Server receives reconnect with same instanceId - accepts (not 409)
Server restores all 3 scope sessions from the SESSION_READY scope list
Extension sends PREPARE_SCOPE for each scope that needs reconfirmation
Verify all 3 scopes are re-established and functional
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to each of the 3 scopes - verify all respond correctly
Verify no scope session data was lost during reconnect
expected_results: Reconnect with same instanceId: accepted (101, no 409)
All 3 scope sessions restored after reconnect
Extension can re-send scope state in SESSION_READY (multi-scope aware)
Scope sessions that were in-flight (streaming) are re-established or cleanly terminated
No STREAM_ERROR for scopes that were active before disconnect
Server log shows: 'Reconnected instance A, restoring N scope sessions'
Epoch counter increments on reconnect but scope session data is preserved
test_scenarios.note: Requires: (1) server persists scopeSessions per instanceId across reconnects, (2) extension sends multi-scope list in SESSION_READY, (3) epoch bump does not clear scopeSessions.

test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Message Ordering Across Scopes
test_scenarios.description: Verify that messages for different scopes sent over the same WebSocket maintain correct ordering per-scope. A stream of messages for scope A should not be interleaved with or reordered relative to scope B messages in a way that corrupts either stream.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker with mocked extension
scenarios: Interleaved sends: app chunk, notebook chunk, app chunk, app done - verify each scope gets correct sequence
Concurrent streams: 2 EXECUTE_REQUESTs (different scopes) in-flight simultaneously - responses arrive in order per scope
Fast scope switch: send to scope A, switch to B, send to B, switch back to A - verify A's in-flight stream is not corrupted

steps: Connect WebSocket, establish 2 scopes: app and notebook:ntb-456def
Scenario 1 - Interleaved messages:
Send STREAM_CHUNK for scope=app (chunk 1)
Send STREAM_CHUNK for scope=notebook (chunk 1)
Send STREAM_CHUNK for scope=app (chunk 2)
Send STREAM_DONE for scope=app
Send STREAM_CHUNK for scope=notebook (chunk 2)
Send STREAM_DONE for scope=notebook
Verify app received: chunk1, chunk2, done (in order, no notebook chunks mixed in)
Verify notebook received: chunk1, chunk2, done (in order, no app chunks mixed in)
Scenario 2 - Concurrent streams:
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST for scope=app (requestId=req-app-1)
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST for scope=notebook (requestId=req-nb-1)
Verify both streams progress independently
Verify req-app-1 response never contains notebook data
Verify req-nb-1 response never contains app data
Scenario 3 - Fast scope switch during stream:
Start EXECUTE_REQUEST for scope=app (long-running stream)
While streaming, switch scope to notebook
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST for scope=notebook
Switch back to app
Verify app stream continues and completes correctly (not cancelled or mixed)
Verify notebook stream also completes correctly
expected_results: Per-scope message ordering is preserved regardless of interleaving
STREAM_CHUNK for scope X is always delivered to scope X's handler
STREAM_DONE for scope X correctly terminates only scope X's stream
Concurrent streams for different scopes do not interfere
Scope switch during an active stream does NOT cancel or corrupt the in-flight stream
requestId uniquely identifies a stream within a scope; no cross-scope collisions
Server log shows scope-tagged message routing for each message
test_scenarios.note: The current implementation uses a single activeStreams Map keyed by requestId. This test validates that requestId is unique per scope session and that routing prefix (scope) is preserved end-to-end.

test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Epoch Bump Doesn't Lose Scope State
test_scenarios.description: Verify that when the server's epoch counter increments (on new connection/reconnect), the scope session state for the reconnecting instance is preserved, not cleared. The epoch is a session-lifecycle marker, not a scope-state reset trigger.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker

steps: Connect WebSocket with instanceId=A, epoch=1
Establish 3 scope sessions: app, app:conv-a1b2c3, notebook:ntb-456def
Record epoch=1 and scope session state (scope IDs, conversation state per scope)
Disconnect (normal close)
Reconnect with same instanceId=A - server assigns epoch=2
Extension sends SESSION_READY with scope list (multi-scope aware)
Verify server restores all 3 scope sessions
Verify epoch=2 in server log but scopeSessions Map still has 3 entries
Verify conversation state (conversationId, responseId, choiceId) per scope is preserved or re-synchronized
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to each scope - verify all 3 work with epoch=2
Disconnect again, reconnect - epoch=3
Verify scope sessions still preserved after epoch=3
Verify epoch counter incremented correctly (1->2->3) but scope state survived each bump
expected_results: Epoch increments on each reconnect (1->2->3)
Scope session state (scopeSessions Map) is NOT cleared on epoch bump
All 3 scopes functional after each reconnect with new epoch
Server log shows: 'Epoch bumped to N, preserving M scope sessions for instance A'
conversationState per scope is re-synced from extension on SESSION_READY if needed
No scope session loss across epoch boundaries
The epoch is used for conflict detection (stale connection identification), not scope state management
test_scenarios.note: Current implementation increments epochCounter on every recordConnection() call. This test ensures that scopeSessions (if implemented) are NOT cleared by the epoch increment - they are separate concerns.

integration_test_plan.overview: Phase 5 integration testing validates that all phases 1-4 changes work correctly together in a staging environment before production rollout. Tests are organized into unit tests (mocked dependencies), integration tests (against staging worker), and manual/end-to-end tests (Chrome extension in browser).

high_pass: TS-003: Server TTL cleanup closes idle connections after 45s

failure_handling.unit_test_failure: Fix the code and re-run unit tests. Do not deploy to staging until unit tests pass.
failure_handling.integration_test_failure: Check staging worker logs for errors. If server-side bug, fix and redeploy to staging. If test bug, fix test and re-run.
failure_handling.409_regression: If TS-007 or TS-012 shows 409 NOT being returned for genuine conflicts, this is a critical regression. Do NOT proceed to production. Investigate server-side connection acceptance logic.
failure_handling.false_409: If TS-005 or TS-010 shows 409 being returned for legitimate reconnects, this is the original bug recurring. Fix server-side instance ID tracking and redeploy.
failure_handling.ttl_not_working: If TS-003 shows connections not being closed after 45s idle, check server-side keepalive loop and stale detection logic.

phase4_test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Single WS Carries 3 Scopes Simultaneously
phase4_test_scenarios.description: Verify that a single WebSocket connection can carry message traffic for 3 different scopes (app, app:conv-X, notebook:Y) concurrently without scope collision or cross-contamination. Each scope maintains its own session state, streaming handlers, and model preparation state.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker with mocked extension that simulates 3 scope sessions

steps: Connect WebSocket with instanceId=A, send SESSION_READY with scope='app'
Send PREPARE_SCOPE for 'app:conv-a1b2c3' - verify SCOPE_READY received, currentScope updated
Send PREPARE_SCOPE for 'notebook:ntb-456def' - verify SCOPE_READY received
Verify server tracks all 3 scopes as active session contexts (not just currentScope)
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST with scope='app' - verify routed to app handler
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST with scope='app:conv-a1b2c3' - verify routed to conversation handler, NOT app handler
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST with scope='notebook:ntb-456def' - verify routed to notebook handler
Verify each requestId's response is delivered to the correct scope's waiting handler
Verify no scope cross-contamination: app:conv response does not leak to app handler
Verify server log shows 3 active scope sessions for this instanceId
expected_results: Single WebSocket connection carries all 3 scopes (no reconnect triggered)
Each scope has independent session state (conversationId, responseId, choiceId per scope)
EXECUTE_REQUEST for app:conv-a1b2c3 does NOT route to app handler
EXECUTE_REQUEST for notebook:ntb-456def does NOT route to app handler
STREAM_CHUNK for notebook scope is not delivered to app:conv handler
Server maintains scopeSessions Map with 3 entries for this instanceId
currentScope reflects the MOST RECENT scope switch, but other scopes remain active
phase4_test_scenarios.note: Requires server-side scopeSessions Map (multi-scope session state). Currently only currentScope is tracked - this test validates the multi-scope enhancement.

phase4_test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Scope Subscribe/Unsubscribe Mid-Session
phase4_test_scenarios.description: Verify that scopes can be dynamically subscribed (PREPARE_SCOPE) and unsubscribed (SCOPE_UNSUBSCRIBE or scope cleanup on navigation away) during an active session, without disrupting other active scopes or the WebSocket connection.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker

steps: Connect WebSocket, establish SESSION_READY with scope='app'
Subscribe to scope 'app:conv-a1b2c3' via PREPARE_SCOPE - verify SCOPE_READY
Subscribe to scope 'notebook:ntb-456def' via PREPARE_SCOPE - verify SCOPE_READY
Verify both scopes are in the active scopeSessions map
Simulate user navigating away from notebook tab (extension sends SCOPE_UNSUBSCRIBE or navigates to different scope)
Verify notebook:ntb-456def is removed from active scopeSessions
Verify app and app:conv-a1b2c3 scopes remain active and functional
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to app:conv-a1b2c3 - verify it still works after notebook unsubscribe
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to app - verify it still works
Subscribe to a NEW scope 'app:conv-new789' - verify it works without affecting existing scopes
Unsubscribe from app:conv-a1b2c3 - verify it's removed, other scopes unaffected
Verify WebSocket remains open throughout all subscribe/unsubscribe operations
expected_results: Scope subscribe (PREPARE_SCOPE -> SCOPE_READY) adds scope to active sessions
Scope unsubscribe removes scope from active sessions without disrupting others
WebSocket connection remains stable throughout (no onclose events)
Active scope count decreases correctly after unsubscribe
Remaining scopes continue to receive messages correctly
No STREAM_ERROR for remaining scopes after another scope unsubscribes
Server log shows scope added/removed events with scope ID
phase4_test_scenarios.note: Requires server-side scope unsubscribe handling. Extension sends SCOPE_UNSUBSCRIBE or navigates away; server cleans up scope session.

phase4_test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Reconnect Preserves All Scope Sessions
phase4_test_scenarios.description: Verify that after a WebSocket reconnect (SW restart, network blip, or deliberate disconnect), all previously active scope sessions are preserved and re-established, not lost. The extension retransmits scope state for each active scope.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker with mocked extension

steps: Connect WebSocket, establish SESSION_READY with scope='app'
Subscribe to app:conv-a1b2c3 and notebook:ntb-456def (3 scopes active)
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to each scope - verify all 3 work
Simulate disconnect: close WebSocket (normal close, code 1000)
Simulate SW restart: extension reinitializes, retrieves instanceId from chrome.storage.session
Extension reconnects with SAME instanceId
Extension sends SESSION_READY with full scope list: ['app', 'app:conv-a1b2c3', 'notebook:ntb-456def']
Server receives reconnect with same instanceId - accepts (not 409)
Server restores all 3 scope sessions from the SESSION_READY scope list
Extension sends PREPARE_SCOPE for each scope that needs reconfirmation
Verify all 3 scopes are re-established and functional
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to each of the 3 scopes - verify all respond correctly
Verify no scope session data was lost during reconnect
expected_results: Reconnect with same instanceId: accepted (101, no 409)
All 3 scope sessions restored after reconnect
Extension can re-send scope state in SESSION_READY (multi-scope aware)
Scope sessions that were in-flight (streaming) are re-established or cleanly terminated
No STREAM_ERROR for scopes that were active before disconnect
Server log shows: 'Reconnected instance A, restoring N scope sessions'
Epoch counter increments on reconnect but scope session data is preserved
phase4_test_scenarios.note: Requires: (1) server persists scopeSessions per instanceId across reconnects, (2) extension sends multi-scope list in SESSION_READY, (3) epoch bump does not clear scopeSessions.

phase4_test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Message Ordering Across Scopes
phase4_test_scenarios.description: Verify that messages for different scopes sent over the same WebSocket maintain correct ordering per-scope. A stream of messages for scope A should not be interleaved with or reordered relative to scope B messages in a way that corrupts either stream.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker with mocked extension
scenarios: Interleaved sends: app chunk, notebook chunk, app chunk, app done - verify each scope gets correct sequence
Concurrent streams: 2 EXECUTE_REQUESTs (different scopes) in-flight simultaneously - responses arrive in order per scope
Fast scope switch: send to scope A, switch to B, send to B, switch back to A - verify A's in-flight stream is not corrupted

steps: Connect WebSocket, establish 2 scopes: app and notebook:ntb-456def
Scenario 1 - Interleaved messages:
Send STREAM_CHUNK for scope=app (chunk 1)
Send STREAM_CHUNK for scope=notebook (chunk 1)
Send STREAM_CHUNK for scope=app (chunk 2)
Send STREAM_DONE for scope=app
Send STREAM_CHUNK for scope=notebook (chunk 2)
Send STREAM_DONE for scope=notebook
Verify app received: chunk1, chunk2, done (in order, no notebook chunks mixed in)
Verify notebook received: chunk1, chunk2, done (in order, no app chunks mixed in)
Scenario 2 - Concurrent streams:
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST for scope=app (requestId=req-app-1)
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST for scope=notebook (requestId=req-nb-1)
Verify both streams progress independently
Verify req-app-1 response never contains notebook data
Verify req-nb-1 response never contains app data
Scenario 3 - Fast scope switch during stream:
Start EXECUTE_REQUEST for scope=app (long-running stream)
While streaming, switch scope to notebook
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST for scope=notebook
Switch back to app
Verify app stream continues and completes correctly (not cancelled or mixed)
Verify notebook stream also completes correctly
expected_results: Per-scope message ordering is preserved regardless of interleaving
STREAM_CHUNK for scope X is always delivered to scope X's handler
STREAM_DONE for scope X correctly terminates only scope X's stream
Concurrent streams for different scopes do not interfere
Scope switch during an active stream does NOT cancel or corrupt the in-flight stream
requestId uniquely identifies a stream within a scope; no cross-scope collisions
Server log shows scope-tagged message routing for each message
phase4_test_scenarios.note: The current implementation uses a single activeStreams Map keyed by requestId. This test validates that requestId is unique per scope session and that routing prefix (scope) is preserved end-to-end.

phase4_test_scenarios.name: Multiplexed Protocol - Epoch Bump Doesn't Lose Scope State
phase4_test_scenarios.description: Verify that when the server's epoch counter increments (on new connection/reconnect), the scope session state for the reconnecting instance is preserved, not cleared. The epoch is a session-lifecycle marker, not a scope-state reset trigger.

setup.environment: Integration test against staging worker

steps: Connect WebSocket with instanceId=A, epoch=1
Establish 3 scope sessions: app, app:conv-a1b2c3, notebook:ntb-456def
Record epoch=1 and scope session state (scope IDs, conversation state per scope)
Disconnect (normal close)
Reconnect with same instanceId=A - server assigns epoch=2
Extension sends SESSION_READY with scope list (multi-scope aware)
Verify server restores all 3 scope sessions
Verify epoch=2 in server log but scopeSessions Map still has 3 entries
Verify conversation state (conversationId, responseId, choiceId) per scope is preserved or re-synchronized
Send EXECUTE_REQUEST to each scope - verify all 3 work with epoch=2
Disconnect again, reconnect - epoch=3
Verify scope sessions still preserved after epoch=3
Verify epoch counter incremented correctly (1->2->3) but scope state survived each bump
expected_results: Epoch increments on each reconnect (1->2->3)
Scope session state (scopeSessions Map) is NOT cleared on epoch bump
All 3 scopes functional after each reconnect with new epoch
Server log shows: 'Epoch bumped to N, preserving M scope sessions for instance A'
conversationState per scope is re-synced from extension on SESSION_READY if needed
No scope session loss across epoch boundaries
The epoch is used for conflict detection (stale connection identification), not scope state management
phase4_test_scenarios.note: Current implementation increments epochCounter on every recordConnection() call. This test ensures that scopeSessions (if implemented) are NOT cleared by the epoch increment - they are separate concerns.
